### Clean up child process after Popen.communicate timeout

Source: https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Doc/library/subprocess.rst

Catch TimeoutExpired when using Popen.communicate() to kill the child process and finish communication. Retrying communicate() ensures output is not lost and populates the returncode attribute.

```python
proc = subprocess.Popen(...)
try:
    outs, errs = proc.communicate(timeout=15)
except TimeoutExpired:
    proc.kill()
    outs, errs = proc.communicate()
```

--------------------------------

### Popen Objects > Popen.communicate()

Source: https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Doc/library/subprocess.rst

Interact with process: Send data to stdin.  Read data from stdout and stderr,
until end-of-file is reached.  Wait for process to terminate and set the
[`returncode`](#subprocess.Popen.returncode) attribute.  The optional *input* argument should be
data to be sent to the child process, or `None`, if no data should be sent
to the child.  If streams were opened in text mode, *input* must be a string.
Otherwise, it must be bytes.

[`communicate()`](#subprocess.Popen.communicate) returns a tuple `(stdout_data, stderr_data)`.
The data will be strings if streams were opened in text mode; otherwise,
bytes.

Note that if you want to send data to the process’s stdin, you need to create
the Popen object with `stdin=PIPE`.  Similarly, to get anything other than
`None` in the result tuple, you need to give `stdout=PIPE` and/or
`stderr=PIPE` too.

If the process does not terminate after *timeout* seconds, a
[`TimeoutExpired`](#subprocess.TimeoutExpired) exception will be raised.  Catching this exception and
retrying communication will not lose any output.  Supplying *input* to a
subsequent post-timeout [`communicate()`](#subprocess.Popen.communicate) call is in undefined behavior
and may become an error in the future.

The child process is not killed if the timeout expires, so in order to
cleanup properly a well-behaved application should kill the child process and
finish communication:

After a call to [`communicate()`](#subprocess.Popen.communicate) raises [`TimeoutExpired`](#subprocess.TimeoutExpired), do
not call [`wait()`](#subprocess.Popen.wait). Use an additional [`communicate()`](#subprocess.Popen.communicate)
call to finish handling pipes and populate the [`returncode`](#subprocess.Popen.returncode)
attribute.

--------------------------------

### Popen.returncode

Source: https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Doc/library/subprocess.rst

The return code of the child process once terminated.

```APIDOC
### Popen.returncode

The child return code, set by `poll()`, `wait()`, or `communicate()`.

#### Type
- `int` or `None` (Read-only)

#### Notes
- Initially `None`. A `None` value indicates the process has not yet terminated.
- A negative value `-N` indicates termination by signal `N` (POSIX only).
- When `shell=True`, reflects the exit status of the shell.
```

--------------------------------

### Popen.returncode

Source: https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Doc/library/subprocess.rst

The child return code. Initially `None`, [`returncode`](#subprocess.Popen.returncode) is set by
a call to the [`poll()`](#subprocess.Popen.poll), [`wait()`](#subprocess.Popen.wait), or [`communicate()`](#subprocess.Popen.communicate) methods
if they detect that the process has terminated.

A `None` value indicates that the process hadn’t yet terminated at the
time of the last method call.

A negative value `-N` indicates that the child was terminated by signal
`N` (POSIX only).

When `shell=True`, the return code reflects the exit status of the shell
itself (e.g. `/bin/sh`), which may map signals to codes such as
`128+N`. See the documentation of the shell (for example, the Bash
manual’s Exit Status) for details.

--------------------------------

### Popen.communicate(input=None, timeout=None)

Source: https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Doc/library/subprocess.rst

Interacts with the process by sending data to stdin and reading data from stdout and stderr until EOF. Waits for the process to terminate and sets the returncode attribute.

```APIDOC
### Signature
`Popen.communicate(input=None, timeout=None)`

### Description
Interact with process: Send data to stdin. Read data from stdout and stderr, until end-of-file is reached. Wait for process to terminate and set the `returncode` attribute.

### Parameters
- **input** (`str` | `bytes` | `None`, optional) - Data to be sent to child process stdin. Must be a string if streams were opened in text mode; otherwise, bytes. Default is `None`.
- **timeout** (`int` | `float` | `None`, optional) - Number of seconds to wait for communication to complete before raising `TimeoutExpired`. Default is `None`.

### Returns
- `tuple` of `(stdout_data, stderr_data)` - Captured output from stdout and stderr as strings (if text mode) or bytes.

### Exceptions
- **TimeoutExpired** - Raised if the process does not terminate after *timeout* seconds. Output is not lost upon catching this exception.
```
